clue.text: Lothario's shrewder when touring gulf state

indicators.note: a tour takes you right round the place you are visiting, so one word travels all the way round the other

parts.note: shrewder and wiser are the same comparative
Oman is the sultanate on the Gulf, the state crosswords reach for most

explanation.walkthrough: Comparatives are useful to a setter: 'shrewder' has to become a whole word rather than an abbreviation, which is a lot of letters handed over at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A womaniser is a habitual seducer, and Lothario is the rake in Rowe's play whose name became the byword for exactly that man.

clue.text: Lead astray some apprentices

indicators.note: 'some' asks for a part of what follows rather than all of it, and a part of a word is a run of its letters

parts.note: the run sits in the middle of apprENTICEs

explanation.walkthrough: Letters buried inside one long word are harder to spot than letters straddling two, because there is no join for the eye to catch on.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to tempt someone off the path they were on, which is what leading them astray amounts to.

clue.text: Unprofitable bank

definitions.meaning: a stretch of time with nothing spare in it, as in the years right after a bad harvest
an aircraft banks by tipping over to one side

explanation.walkthrough: Two words, no indicator and nothing to take apart: that shape is nearly always two definitions, and here the second is a pilot's verb, not a high street noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean year is one with no profit in it, and an aircraft banks by tipping to one side, which is to lean.

clue.text: Test top of rainwater tank

parts.note: a test of your ability is a challenge

indicators.note: the top of a thing is the end you meet first, so only the opening letter of the word beneath it is taken

parts.note: the first letter of rainwater

explanation.walkthrough: The tank in the surface is a water butt; the tank in the definition is the Army's, and that switch is the whole clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Challenger is the British Army's main battle tank, so the definition names the answer by the class of machine it belongs to.

clue.text: Histrionic pub server describes age

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw all the way round it, so one piece is drawn round another

parts.note: the optic is the measure clamped under a spirits bottle behind the bar
an era is an age

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pub server' sounds like a person and is really a piece of bar equipment, which is where this one hides.
explanation.definitionFit: Histrionic means overplayed in the manner of the stage, and operatic carries the same charge of theatrical excess.

clue.text: Motorway network in Italian city

parts.note: the M1 spelled out as two characters, motorway one
a LAN is the local area network wired into any office

explanation.walkthrough: Two conventions worth banking here: a motorway becomes MI, letter beside letter, and a network in a grid is almost always the office LAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Milan is the northern Italian city of fashion and finance, so the definition places the answer by country and size.

clue.text: More recent winner of Pop Idol seen by European river

indicators.note: to be seen by someone is to be standing next to them, so these letters simply take their place alongside

parts.note: Will Young won the first series of Pop Idol
E is the standard short form of European
R is river on any map

explanation.walkthrough: This one asks you to remember a talent show result from 2002, and then only wants the surname of the singer who won it.
explanation.definitionFit: Younger and more recent are the same comparative: a younger building is one put up more recently than the rest.

clue.text: Man taps phone program that is …

parts.note: the pair over a sink are labelled cold and hot
an app is the program you run on a phone
i.e. is the Latin id est, that is

explanation.walkthrough: Taps are a setter's way of asking for the two letters on the sink, and the dots at the end only pass the sentence on to 10 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A chappie is a chap with a friendly ending stuck on, British slang for an ordinary bloke and so simply a man.

clue.text: Study purpose for return to hospital?

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it
a mission is the purpose someone is sent out with

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark is the setter admitting that his definition describes the answer rather than swapping for it word for word.
explanation.definitionFit: A readmission is a patient being taken into hospital again, so the definition describes the event the word names.

clue.text: … surprisingly neat epic game

indicators.note: a surprise is something arriving in an order nobody expected, and that is what happens to these letters

parts.note: the eight letters of both words are the raw material

explanation.walkthrough: The dots leading in from 8 across are surface only — each clue stands on its own — and the answer is the card game a solitary player deals out.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is the card game one player deals alone, the British name for solitaire, so 'game' names it by the class it sits in.

clue.text: Burglar I attacked holding rope

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside your grip, and these words are keeping what is wanted inside them

parts.note: the run starts in burgLAR and finishes in I ATtacked

explanation.walkthrough: The words read as a snatch of courtroom testimony, and that capital I is exactly what stops the eye seeing a run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is the lasso a cowboy throws, a length of rope finished with a running noose.

clue.text: Unsuitable pix? I need ten developed

indicators.note: a negative is developed until a picture nobody could see comes out of it, and these letters come out in a fresh order

parts.note: pix is the trade's slang for photographs
the three small words go into the mix exactly as they stand

explanation.walkthrough: The whole surface is a darkroom, so the instruction looks like part of the picture rather than the order it is giving.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexpedient means not advisable in the circumstances, so 'unsuitable' catches it in the everyday sense of the wrong thing to do.

clue.text: Film title about independent group of soldiers in a pickle

indicators.note: when one thing is written about another it goes all the way round it, so the single letter drops inside

parts.note: a pic is a film, the trade's own shortening
to call a thing is to give it its title
I is independent on a ballot paper
LI is the Light Infantry, as in the DLI

explanation.walkthrough: Being in a pickle means being in trouble, which is the trap: the pickle wanted here is the jar of yellow relish.
explanation.definitionFit: Piccalilli is the mustard-yellow relish of chopped vegetables sold in jars, which is one particular kind of pickle.

clue.text: Pastor with bug is tipsy in posh boozer

indicators.note: somebody tipsy cannot walk a straight line, and these letters will not stay in the line they were given

parts.note: the six letters of the clergyman go into the mix
the insect's three letters join them

explanation.walkthrough: A tipsy pastor is a good enough picture to stop you counting, and the count is the tell: the two words hold exactly nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastropub is a pub that takes its kitchen seriously, so 'posh boozer' is the plain-spoken name for the same establishment.

clue.text: Conference maybe cut back we hear

indicators.note: what we take in by ear is a sound, and one sound can be written down in more than one way

parts.note: to pare back is to cut, and PARE said aloud is spelled the other way

explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' is the setter flagging an example rather than a synonym, since Conference is one named variety among many.
explanation.definitionFit: Conference is a named variety of pear, so the definition points at the answer through one example, which 'maybe' politely admits.

clue.text: Writer raised hesitation over old railway worker

indicators.note: letters raised in a down clue are read from the bottom upwards, so the pair arrives the other way round
one thing over another lies on top of it, which in a down entry means it comes first

parts.note: er is the noise you make while you hesitate
the porter who carried luggage on the platform, a job the railways no longer keep

explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' is not the usual O here: it is telling you the railway job belongs to another era, when somebody carried your case to the train.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter writes the news for a paper, so 'writer' defines the answer by the wider trade it belongs to.

clue.text: Hold fast having caught fish

parts.note: c is caught on a cricket scorecard
the ling is a long fish of the cod family

explanation.walkthrough: C for caught comes off a cricket scorecard, and the ling is the cod-family fish that grids keep permanently in stock.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling is to grip something and not let go, which is holding fast in the sense of gripping rather than tying.

clue.text: See you appearing regularly in Chicago

indicators.note: something that turns up regularly comes at fixed intervals, so take every second letter and skip the rest

parts.note: ChIcAgO, taking the first letter and every other one after it

explanation.walkthrough: The word serves as both hello and goodbye in Italian; 'See you' picks the parting one, and the city is only there to carry the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciao is the Italian farewell English has borrowed, and 'see you' is the same casual sign-off to a friend.

clue.text: A trusty plan devised for what Ferris Bueller does

indicators.note: to devise is to make something new out of the material you have, and the material here is a handful of letters

parts.note: all eleven letters of the phrase are the raw material

explanation.walkthrough: Ferris Bueller's Day Off is a whole film about a boy skiving school, so the definition is a clause pointing at one action.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferris Bueller spends his famous Day Off skiving school, and to play truant is precisely that: staying away without leave.

clue.text: Time chairman originally enters City office

indicators.note: what a word is originally is how it starts, so only its opening letter is wanted

parts.note: an age is a long stretch of time

indicators.note: to enter a building is to go inside it, so the letter goes in among the ones already there

parts.note: NY is New York City
the first letter of chairman, which is what goes into NY

explanation.walkthrough: The city wanted is New York; the boardroom surface leans on that capital C to keep you looking at the Square Mile instead.
explanation.definitionFit: An agency is the office a business trades from — a travel agency, an ad agency — so the two words name the same premises.

clue.text: Officer commanding old volunteers left base

parts.note: OC is the army's officer commanding
the Territorial Army, the volunteer force renamed the Army Reserve in 2014
L is left

explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' is not a barracks: octal is the base-eight counting system computing grew up on, and the parade ground is there to hide that sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Octal is the base-eight number system, so 'base' is the mathematician's sense of the word rather than the soldier's.

clue.text: Tax return on investment after 31 days

indicators.note: a thing that comes after another is written behind it, so this piece follows the one already down

parts.note: October is a 31-day month, shortened to Oct
ROI is the financier's return on investment

explanation.walkthrough: A month clued by its length is a standing device: seven of them have 31 days, so the crossing letters are what pick October out.
explanation.definitionFit: An octroi is a local duty charged on goods entering a town, which makes it one particular kind of tax.

clue.text: At work dealing with article and book

parts.note: a book on birds is a book dealing with birds
the definite article
Job is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.walkthrough: Two staples in one clue: an article is the grammarian's THE, and a book is very often one of the Bible's.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on the job is to be at work, the idiom taken whole, as a workman on the job is one currently doing it.

clue.text: Tough husband aboard boat

indicators.note: aboard means on the vessel and therefore inside it, so the letter is stowed within the boat

parts.note: a tug is the little boat that shoves ships about
H is husband in the abbreviation book

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tough' is a noun in the definition while the surface reads it as an adjective, and that shift is the whole of the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough, as a noun, is a violent bruiser of a man, which is exactly what a thug is.

clue.text: Meat spread all around bone

parts.note: pate is the meat spread you put on toast

indicators.note: to bring a ship around is to turn it to face the other way, and the word in front of it turns the same way

parts.note: the little word taken whole, before it is turned

explanation.walkthrough: Meat spread all around sounds like a buffet table, which is what keeps the next word looking like description rather than instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella is the kneecap, so 'bone' defines the answer by naming the class of thing it is.

clue.text: Which Spanish friend finally abandoned a Peruvian?

indicators.note: what a word does finally is end, and giving up that end leaves it one letter shorter

parts.note: que is the Spanish for which
CHUM is a friend, and its closing M is abandoned
the little word joins on at the end as it stands

explanation.walkthrough: Setters lean on the Spanish everybody half-knows, and the question mark admits that a Quechua speaker is only one sort of Peruvian.
explanation.definitionFit: Quechua is the Andean language of the Inca and the people who speak it, so a Peruvian is one fair example.
